String operations

Source: R/strings.R
z3_strings.Rd

Z3 strings are sequences of Unicode characters. Character literals in R are converted to Z3 string values exactly. Positions are 0-based, as in SMT-LIB.

Usage

z3_length(s)

z3_contains(s, t)

z3_prefixof(t, s)

z3_suffixof(t, s)

z3_substr(s, offset, length)

z3_str_at(s, i)

z3_indexof(s, t, offset = 0)

z3_replace(s, src, dst)

z3_str_to_int(s)

z3_int_to_str(x)

z3_str_lt(s, t)

z3_str_le(s, t)

Arguments

s, t, src, dst

String expressions or R strings.

offset, length, i

Int expressions or R whole numbers.

x

An Int (for z3_int_to_str()) or String expression.

Value

A z3_expr.

Details

  • z3_length(): number of characters (an Int).

  • z3_concat(): concatenation (see z3_bitvectors; it also joins strings).

  • z3_contains(s, t), z3_prefixof(t, s), z3_suffixof(t, s): containment tests. Note the SMT-LIB argument order: z3_prefixof(t, s) is "t is a prefix of s".

  • z3_substr(s, offset, length), z3_str_at(s, i): substrings.

  • z3_indexof(s, t, offset): first position of t in s at or after offset, or -1.

  • z3_replace(s, src, dst): replaces the first occurrence of src.

  • z3_str_to_int(), z3_int_to_str(): conversion between decimal strings and non-negative integers (-1 for invalid strings).

  • z3_str_lt(), z3_str_le(): lexicographic order by code point.

Examples

ctx <- z3_context()
s <- z3_string(ctx, "s")
sol <- z3_solver(ctx)
z3_add(sol, z3_length(s) == 5, z3_prefixof("ab", s), z3_contains(s, "zz"))
z3_check(sol)
#> [1] "sat"
z3_value(z3_eval(z3_model(sol), s))
#> [1] "abAzz"
